title: Dietary supplementation with Kelussia odoratissima extract improves growth performance and modulates intestinal cytokine‐related gene expression in zebrafish (Danio rerio)
content:
Abstract

Kelussia odoratissima (wild celery) is an endemic medicinal plant containing diverse bioactive phytochemicals; however, its potential as a dietary additive in fish has not previously been investigated. This study evaluated the effects of dietary hydroethanolic K. odoratissima extract (KOE) on growth performance, feed utilization, and intestinal cytokine-related gene expression in zebrafish (Danio rerio). A total of 600 fish (initial body weight: 210 ± 10 mg) were randomly allocated to 15 tanks (three replicate tanks per treatment) and fed five experimental diets supplemented with 0, 2.5, 5, 10, or 15 g KOE kg−1 diet for 56 days. Dietary KOE significantly improved growth performance and feed utilization (p < 0.05). Fish fed 10 g KOE kg−1 exhibited the highest final body weight (660 ± 10 mg), specific growth rate (2.10% day−1), and protein efficiency ratio (1.29), together with the lowest feed conversion ratio (1.53). Quadratic regression suggested that dietary inclusion levels of approximately 10–11 g KOE kg−1 were associated with the greatest biological responses under the present experimental conditions. Survival remained high (94–100%) and did not differ significantly among treatments (p > 0.05). Dietary KOE upregulated intestinal tnf-α and il-1β expression while downregulating il-10 and tgf-β1, indicating modulation of intestinal cytokine-related gene expression. These transcriptional responses should not be interpreted as direct evidence of enhanced immune function. Overall, dietary KOE improved growth performance and modulated intestinal cytokine-related gene expression in zebrafish. Further studies incorporating functional immune assessments, histopathology, and validation in commercially important aquaculture species are required before practical applications can be recommended.
